apps.name: Paruto Kids World
apps.tagline: An illustrated village where little ones learn and play with Jas, Jay and baby Joe.
apps.description: A browser-based illustrated village for children aged 2–5. Kids walk through six places with Jas, Jay and baby Joe and choose from over 40 activities: letters, tracing and counting, music and dance, animals and life cycles, feelings, staying safe and Bible stories, plus a Colour Workshop for drawing. It works offline, with no ads, no social feeds and no endless scrolling, and a grown-up gate keeps the parent area separate.

apps.name: Ivra
apps.tagline: Accounting and payroll for Nigerian businesses, with the tax worked out.
apps.description: One set of books for invoices, bills, expenses, banking, tax and payroll, on your phone or computer. It works out PAYE on the 2026 bands, pension, NHF, NSITF and ITF, emails payslips, keeps VAT and withholding tax as sums you can follow to the due date, and plans each project's costs against the price the client pays, with the margin you're heading for. Built like a ledger: every entry balances, posted entries are never edited, and closed months stay locked. Invite-only for now.
highlights: Payroll with PAYE, pension and levies, and payslips in one tap
Invoices in naira or dollars, with VAT and withholding tax

apps.name: Hyperspeed Rail
apps.tagline: A concept maglev network for Nigeria on real terrain, and a game you can drive.
apps.description: A concept double-track maglev network for Nigeria: 11 lines and 54 stations drawn on real terrain in the browser, with trains running both ways every 30 minutes and a journey planner between any two stations. Drive the trains, take the daily challenge, build a career and play the State League, redraw lines in build puzzles, or run the network and see whether the fares cover the costs. A concept, not an official plan; costs are benchmarks from real projects.

apps.name: ARCLIGHT
apps.tagline: An anti-gravity racer for the browser, with every mesh and sound generated in code.
apps.description: An original anti-gravity racing game built with Three.js. Race fourteen circuits in either direction, eleven of them across Nigeria, from Lagos Lagoon and Abuja's Aso Rock to Kano's ancient city, Calabar's Carnival and Benin City's ancient kingdom, with airbrakes, boost pads and weapons against skill-based AI. Take on the Naija Cup, the daily challenge, a weekly tournament and leagues, race a friend live, and earn medals and liveries. Every mesh, texture and sound is generated in code.

apps.name: Repwise
apps.tagline: A free workout coach that shows every move, with no sign-up.
apps.description: A free fitness app you can install on any phone or desktop. Coach Remy demonstrates each exercise, counts your reps and keeps your progress. apps.name: Anansi: Swing City
apps.tagline: A 3D web-swinging game: swing across Lagos, London or any city you name, and switch the lights back on.
apps.description: Anansi, the West African spider trickster, is now a web-slinger, and Dr. Blackout has cut the city's power. Swing through an endless 3D city, starting in Lagos from Lagos Island over the Third Mainland Bridge to Eko Atlantic, smash drones, bounce on danfos and grab power cells until the skyline shouts UP NEPA! Choose Lagos, Abuja, Accra, Cape Town, London, New York or Dubai, or type any city's name, and hear local slang from the bus conductors to the rescued crowds. Missions, web-zips and a city passport keep every run fresh, and Swing City Lite, a 2D version, runs on older phones and slow connections.

apps.name: Project Meridian
apps.tagline: Ninety-nine maps burned. One kept.
apps.description: A sailor drew a hundred maps and burned ninety-nine. The one he kept had crossed the ocean a thousand times by lamplight before it ever touched the sea.
highlights: Drawn by lamplight

apps.tagline: A letter you can walk into.
apps.description: A child was handed a letter written only in lines and corners. She folded it once, then twice, and stepped inside.
highlights: Folded twice

apps.name: Project Lantern
apps.tagline: The lamp that shows where to look.
apps.description: In a village without a doctor, a woman carried a lamp from door to door. The lamp healed no one. It only showed her where to look.
highlights: Door to door

apps.name: Project Tempo
apps.tagline: A diary that keeps pace.
apps.description: A runner never wrote a word, yet each night her diary held the whole race, every stride exactly where it fell.
highlights: Every stride where it fell

apps.name: Project Harbor
apps.tagline: The tide that brings back the nets.
apps.description: A fisherman counted his nets each morning and found nothing missing. Then the tide came in carrying three he had never known were gone.
highlights: Counted every morning

apps.name: Project Willow
apps.tagline: The tree that taught the wind to sing.
apps.description: An old woman hung a single reed beneath the willow by her gate. Every child who passed stopped to make it sing, and by summer the whole lane could hum her tunes, though none of them remembered being taught.
highlights: One reed by the gate

apps.name: Project Cairn
apps.tagline: Every stone a witness.
apps.description: A mason laid a stone at every turn of the road. Years later, travellers who had never met him followed the stones to his door and asked for him by name.
highlights: A stone at every turn

apps.name: Project Loom
apps.tagline: The loom before the cloth.
apps.description: The weaver made no cloth at all that first year. She built the loom, and every cloth that came off it after carried the same quiet thread.
highlights: One loom

apps.name: Project Heron
apps.tagline: What the heron carries, the river never hears.
apps.description: Every morning a heron left the house with nothing and came home with word from the far bank. The river ran beside it all day and never learned what it carried.
highlights: Out at dawn
Home by dusk

apps.name: Project Vigil
apps.tagline: The watchman who never sleeps.
apps.description: A watchman stood at the gate through every hour of the night. He never dozed and never guessed. He moved only when the sky showed the sign he had been waiting for.
highlights: Every hour of the night
